definition_en: the process of doing something, or a thing that is done
core_image: 一只手按下开关，机器立刻开始转动
scene: 孩子被困在火里，是迅速的救援行动救了他。Quick action saved the child from the fire.
sceneCN: 这里的 action 是「行动」（第 1 个义项：做事的过程）；句意是迅速的行动救了孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「行动；表演」
由词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「活跃的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「活动」
由词根加动词后缀构成，义为「激活」

senses.title: The doing of something
senses.definition: the process of doing something in order to reach a result
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到结果而去做某事的过程
senses.example: The rescue required fast action.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援需要迅速行动。
senses.why: The Latin noun actio comes from agere, to drive, so action is the force that sets a thing in motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 actio 出自 agere（驱动），所以 action 是让事情动起来的那股力。

senses.title: The effect of a substance
senses.definition: the way a drug, chemical or force produces an effect
senses.definitionCN: 药物、化学品或某种力量产生效果的方式
senses.example: The action of the poison is very fast.
senses.exampleCN: 这种毒物的发作非常快。
senses.why: A thing that works on another is also driving it, so the noun extends from people to medicines and acids.
senses.whyCN: 一物作用于另一物，也是一种驱动，于是这个名词从人扩展到药物与酸液。

senses.title: A case brought to court
senses.definition: a legal process asking a court to decide a claim
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院裁决某项主张的法律程序
senses.example: She brought an action against the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这家公司提起了诉讼。
senses.why: In law a deed becomes a formal step, and the court calls that step an action.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，一件事变成一道正式程序，法院就把这道程序叫作 action。

senses.title: Fighting in a battle
senses.definition: active fighting between armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量之间的实际交战
senses.example: He was wounded in action near the border.
senses.exampleCN: 他在边境附近的战斗中负伤。
senses.why: Driving becomes driving an attack, so the same noun names the place where force is used in earnest.
senses.whyCN: 「驱动」变成「驱动进攻」，同一个名词便指真正动用武力的场合。

intro.en: The noun is Latin, built from the verb that means to drive or do.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语，由表示「驱动、做」的动词构成。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to lead or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、带领或做。

items.en: actus named a deed or a movement.
items.cn: actus 指行为或动作。

items.en: actio named the doing itself.
items.cn: actio 指「做」这一行为本身。

items.en: action entered English for deeds, and later for legal and military steps.
items.cn: action 在十四世纪进入英语，指行为，后来又指法律与军事上的行动。

items.en: it now also names the effect of a drug or a machine.
items.cn: 如今它也指药物或机器产生的作用。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second is other words for deeds and operation.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的表示行为与运作的词。

entries.definition: a step taken for a purpose

normal.cn: action 是 act 的名词，正如 motion 是 move 的名词。

normal.cn: take action 是最常见的动词搭配。

normal.en: legal action turns the word into a court case.

normal.cn: killed in action 是阵亡的军事说法。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手按下开关，轮子开始转。

abstract.cn: 想象法庭里一项主张变成一桩案件。

examples.en: Immediate action prevented a worse accident.
examples.cn: 立即行动防止了更严重的事故。

examples.en: The action of the acid on the metal was visible.

examples.en: The couple took legal action over the noise.
examples.cn: 这对夫妇就噪声问题提起了诉讼。

definition_en: the act of making something start working or become chemically active
core_image: 一枚钥匙插进锁孔，指示灯由红转绿
scene: 警报被激活后，整栋楼的人都醒了。The activation of the alarm woke the whole building.
sceneCN: 这里的 activation 是「启动」（第 1 个义项：使设备开始工作）；句意是警报启动惊醒了全楼。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「激活；启动」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「活跃的；活性的」

由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「活动；活性」

senses.title: Starting a device or system
senses.definition: the act of making a machine, account or system begin to work
senses.definitionCN: 使机器、账户或系统开始工作的行为
senses.example: Activation of the card takes a single phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 激活这张卡只需打一个电话。
senses.why: The verb activate means to make active, and the noun names that switch from dormant to working.
senses.whyCN: 动词 activate 意为「使进入活动状态」，名词便指从休眠转为运转的那一下。

senses.title: Making a substance chemically active
senses.definition: the process of giving a molecule or cell the energy to react
senses.definitionCN: 使分子或细胞获得反应所需能量的过程
senses.example: The activation of the enzyme requires a small amount of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶的活化需要少量热量。
senses.why: In chemistry the same switch is pushed at the molecular level: a particle goes from inert to ready.
senses.whyCN: 在化学里，同一个开关被按在分子层面：微粒从惰性变为待发。

intro.en: The noun is built on the Latin act root with a suffix meaning to make.
intro.cn: 这个名词建在拉丁语 act 词根上，带一个表示「使……」的后缀。

items.cn: active 作为表示行动、活跃的形容词进入英语。

abstract.en: Think of a phone screen lighting up at a first touch.
abstract.cn: 想象手机屏幕在第一次触碰时亮起。

examples.cn: 新账户的激活只需一分钟。

definition_zh: 积极的；主动的；活跃的；活性的
definition_en: doing things regularly, or working and having an effect
core_image: 清晨的操场上，已经有人在跑第二圈
scene: 这座火山沉寂多年，但至今仍然活跃。The volcano is still active after centuries.
sceneCN: 这里的 active 是「活跃的」（第 2 个义项：仍在活动、未停息）；句意是这座火山几百年后仍然活跃。

pos.zh: 积极的；主动的；活跃的；活性的

senses.title: Doing things rather than watching
senses.definition: taking part in things and making effort rather than waiting
senses.definitionCN: 参与其中并付出努力，而不是等着
senses.example: She is an active member of the reading club.
senses.exampleCN: 她是读书会的活跃成员。
senses.why: The Latin activus says able to act, so the first sense simply marks a person who acts instead of idling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 activus 意为「能行动的」，所以第一个义项就是标记一个动手去做、而非闲着的人。

senses.title: Still working or moving
senses.definition: continuing to operate, especially of a volcano, market or machine
senses.definitionCN: 仍在运转，尤指火山、市场或机器
senses.example: The market was active all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午市场都很活跃。
senses.why: Able to act also describes things: a volcano that still erupts or a market that still trades keeps the same power.
senses.whyCN: 「能行动」也用来形容事物：还在喷发的火山、还在交易的市场，保留着同一股力量。

senses.title: Having a chemical effect
senses.definition: producing an effect in a chemical or biological system
senses.definitionCN: 在化学或生物系统中产生作用的
senses.example: The active ingredient relieves pain within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 有效成分几分钟内就能止痛。
senses.why: In medicine and chemistry the acting force is invisible, so active names whatever in a mixture actually does the work.
senses.whyCN: 在医药与化学里，起作用的力量看不见，于是 active 指混合物中真正干活的那一部分。

intro.en: The adjective comes from Latin activus, able to act, built on the verb to drive.

normal.en: the active voice makes the doer the subject of the sentence.

definition_en: in a way that shows effort and direct participation
core_image: 讨论桌旁，一只手总是第一个举起来
scene: 每次课堂讨论，她都积极发言。She actively participates in every class discussion.

senses.title: With direct personal effort
senses.definition: by taking part and putting in effort rather than staying passive
senses.definitionCN: 以参与并出力的方式，而不是被动旁观
senses.example: The students actively shaped the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们积极参与制定了新规则。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's idea of being able to act and applies it to the manner of doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词带着形容词「能行动」的意思，落在做事的方式上。

senses.title: With continuing energy
senses.definition: in a way that keeps operating or growing strongly
senses.definitionCN: 以持续运转或强劲增长的方式
senses.example: The company is actively recruiting engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司正在积极招聘工程师。
senses.why: Effort can also be steady rather than sudden, so the adverb describes an ongoing push rather than a single step.
senses.whyCN: 努力也可以是持续而非一时的，于是这个副词描述的是不断推进，而不是单独一步。

intro.cn: 形容词词干加方式词尾，构成这个副词。

latinIntro.en: The root agere also gives agent and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 agere 也给出 agent 与 agenda。

definition_zh: 积极分子；活动家；行动主义者
definition_en: a person who works hard to bring about political or social change
core_image: 一个人举着标语站在队伍最前面，高声喊出口号
scene: 那位环保活动家站在工厂门口，举牌要求停止排污。The environmental activist stood at the factory gate holding a sign.
sceneCN: 这里的 activist 是「活动家」（第 1 个义项：为政治或社会改变奔走的人）；句中指为环保奔走的那位人士。

derivatives.zh: 把后缀 -ist 换成 -ism，指「行动主义、积极行动」
同源基础动词，义为「行动；起作用」
同源形容词，义为「积极的、活跃的」
同源名词，义为「活动」
同源动词，义为「使启动、激活」

senses.title: A campaigner for change
senses.definition: a person who works to bring about political or social change
senses.definitionCN: 为促成政治或社会改变而持续奔走的人
senses.example: The activist spent years fighting for cleaner water.
senses.exampleCN: 这位活动家为争取更清洁的水源奋斗了多年。
senses.why: The -ist suffix marks a person, and the base active marks doing, so an activist is literally one who keeps doing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 表示人，词干 active 表示在做，因此 activist 字面就是「一直去做的人」，落在社会运动里便是活动家。

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.definition: placed before a noun to describe a group or policy that campaigns for change
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，形容某个团体或主张带有行动主义色彩
senses.example: The activist wing of the party demanded a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 党内的行动主义一派要求进行表决。
senses.why: English often drops the noun into an attributive slot, so the name of the person becomes a label for the group.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表人的名词直接挪到名词前作定语，于是「那个人」就变成「那一派的」标签。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for doing, fitted with two endings that mark tendency and person.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「做」的拉丁词根，接上表倾向与表人的两个词尾合成。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to do or to act.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、做、行动。

items.en: activus described something full of movement.
items.cn: activus 形容充满活动的、活跃的。

items.en: activiste named a supporter of a cause in motion.
items.cn: activiste 指某个事业的积极推动者。

items.en: activist entered English through political writing.
items.cn: activist 经政治评论进入英语。

items.en: it now covers anyone who campaigns, from unions to climate groups.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖从工会到气候团体的各类推动者。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second names people who push for a cause.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的表示推动某项事业的人。

entries.definition: one who works for a cause
one who speaks for a cause
one who seeks to improve a system

normalIntro.en: act plus ive plus ist builds the person who keeps acting for a cause.
normalIntro.cn: act 加 ive 再加 ist，拼出那个为某项事业持续行动的人。

normal.en: The ist ending almost always marks a person, as in artist and scientist.
normal.cn: ist 结尾几乎总表示人，如 artist、scientist。

normal.en: An activist is not just active; the person acts on a public issue.
normal.cn: 活动家不只是 active，而是针对公共议题持续行动的人。

normal.en: Political activist is the most frequent collocation.
normal.cn: political activist 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The plural activists takes a plain s.
normal.cn: 复数 activists 直接加 s。

normal.en: Activists usually work in groups, so the plural is very common.
normal.cn: 活动家通常成群行动，所以复数形式很常用。

abstract.en: See one figure standing ahead of a crowd with a placard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人举着牌子，站在人群最前面。

abstract.en: Picture a long meeting where one voice keeps insisting.
abstract.cn: 想象一场长会上，总有一个声音坚持不放。

abstract.en: Think of a chain of small acts that finally changes a rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一连串小行动最终改变了一条规则。

examples.en: Police released the activist after questioning.
examples.cn: 警方讯问后释放了这名活动人士。

examples.en: She became an activist while at university.
examples.cn: 她在大学期间成为积极分子。

examples.en: The activist argued that the law was unfair.
examples.cn: 这位活动家主张那条法律并不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维斯特」——阿克提着标语牌，维斯特跟着喊口号，二人都成了活动家。

root: 拉丁语 agere（驱动、做）→ activus（活跃的）→ 法语 activiste → 英语 activist；本义是「持续去做的人」，十九世纪起专指推动社会或政治改变的人。

sensesIntro.en: One word names the person and, before a noun, the camp that person belongs to.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指那个人，也能放在名词前指那个人所属的一派。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lone figure holding a sign in front of a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群之前，一个人独自举着标语。

branches.en: a person who pushes for reform
a group labelled by that spirit
branches.cn: 以这种精神为标签的团体

branches.en: the voice at the front of a crowd
branches.cn: 人群最前面发声的那个声音

branches.en: person and cause folded into one label
branches.cn: 人与事业合成一个标签

branches.en: the attributive slot before a noun

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, two endings, and one person is born.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的拉丁动词，加上两个词尾，就造出了一个人。

latinIntro.en: The same root gives act, action, active and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词根还给出 act、action、active 与 agenda。

definition_zh: 活动；活跃；生理或化学活动
definition_en: something that people do, or the state of being busy and moving
core_image: 操场上孩子奔跑、球在空中飞，一切都在动
scene: 雨停之后，操场上的活动一下子多了起来。Activity on the playground picked up once the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里的 activity 是「活动」（第 1 个义项：人们为兴趣或目的去做的事）；句中指操场上热闹起来的那些活动。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「行动」
同源形容词，义为「活跃的」
同源副词，义为「积极地」
同源动词，义为「启动、激活」
同源名词，义为「活动家」

senses.title: Something people do
senses.definition: a thing that people do for pleasure, for learning or for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 人们为了娱乐、学习或某个目的而去做的事情
senses.example: Swimming is my favourite summer activity.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳是我最喜欢的夏季活动。
senses.why: The noun of active simply names whatever keeps a person in motion, so any organized thing people do is an activity.
senses.whyCN: active 的名词直接指「让人动起来的事」，于是任何有组织的、人们去做的事都叫 activity。

senses.title: The state of being busy
senses.definition: the condition of being busy, energetic or full of movement
senses.definitionCN: 忙碌、有活力或充满运动的状态
senses.example: The market showed strong activity all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午市场都表现得十分活跃。
senses.why: The same noun also measures the degree of movement rather than naming one event, which is how economists talk about markets.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词还能衡量「动的程度」而不指某件具体的事，经济学家说市场活跃正是这个用法。

senses.title: Work inside a living system
senses.definition: the working of a body, organ or system
senses.definitionCN: 身体、器官或某个系统内部的运作
senses.example: The scan revealed unusual activity in his brain.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示他的大脑里有异常活动。
senses.why: Doctors extended the word from what a person does to what cells and nerves do, because both are forms of working.
senses.whyCN: 医生把这个词从「人做的事」扩展到「细胞和神经做的事」，因为二者都是「在运作」。

intro.en: A Latin adjective for busy was turned into a noun of state, then borrowed into English.
intro.cn: 拉丁语里表示「忙」的形容词先变成表状态的名词，再被借入英语。

items.en: agere meant to drive or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: activus described a person or thing in motion.
items.cn: activus 形容处于运动之中的人或物。

items.en: activitas named the state of being so.
items.cn: activitas 指处于这种状态。

items.en: activite carried the noun into medieval French.
items.cn: activite 把这个名词带进中古法语。

items.en: activity first meant energy, then came to mean a particular pursuit.
items.cn: activity 先指精力充沛，后来才指某项具体的活动。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second names kinds of doing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的表示「所做的事」的词。

entries.definition: an activity one spends time on

normalIntro.en: active plus ity turns the adjective of doing into the name of a thing done.
normalIntro.cn: active 加 ity，把「活跃的」变成「所做的事」。

normal.en: The ity ending makes abstract nouns of state, as in ability and reality.
normal.cn: ity 结尾把词变成表状态的名词，如 ability、reality。

normal.en: One activity, two activities: y turns into ies.
normal.cn: 单数 activity，复数 activities，y 变 ies。

normal.en: Physical activity is the standard phrase in health writing.
normal.cn: physical activity 是健康类文章里的标准说法。

normal.en: Economic activity measures how busy a market is.
normal.cn: economic activity 衡量市场有多忙。

normal.en: Brain activity is the scientific use of the same noun.
normal.cn: brain activity 是这个词的科学用法。

abstract.en: See a playground where every child is moving at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个操场，所有孩子同时在动。

abstract.en: Picture a chart line jumping up and down all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线整天上下跳动。

abstract.en: Think of tiny sparks running along a nerve.
abstract.cn: 想象细小的火花沿着神经奔跑。

examples.en: Reading is a quiet activity that needs no company.
examples.cn: 阅读是一种不需要同伴的安静活动。

examples.en: The town shows little activity after dark.
examples.cn: 天黑之后镇上就没什么动静了。

examples.en: Doctors measured the activity in his brain.
examples.cn: 医生测量了他大脑的活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维提」——阿克一提起维提这个名字，整个人就活跃起来，活动也多了。

root: 拉丁语 activitas（活跃状态），源自 activus（活跃的）与 agere（驱动、做）；由「处于活动之中」引申为具体的某项活动与生理活动。

sensesIntro.en: One noun covers a hobby, a busy market and the firing of nerves.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，既指爱好，也指市场的繁忙与神经的放电。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a playground in full motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：满场都在动的操场。

branches.en: a hobby or organized thing to do
how busy a place or market is
signals moving inside a body
doing by one person and by a whole market
branches.cn: 一个人与整个市场的「在动」

branches.en: movement measured rather than named
branches.cn: 被测量的动而不是被命名的事

intro.en: A root of doing, an adjective ending and a noun of state build the word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的词根，加形容词词尾，再加表状态的名词词尾，构成这个词。

latinIntro.en: The family also gives action, actor, agenda and agent.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族还给出 action、actor、agenda 与 agent。

definition_en: a person who performs in plays or films, or a person who takes part in an event
core_image: 聚光灯下，一个人站在舞台中央念出最后一句台词
scene: 导演喊停之后，那位演员仍站在原处不动。The actor stayed still after the director called a stop.
sceneCN: 这里的 actor 是「演员」（第 1 个义项：在舞台或银幕上表演的人）；句中指拍戏时入戏未出的人。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「表演；行动」
同源名词，义为「行动」
同源名词，义为「表演；演技」
加阴性后缀构成，义为「女演员」
同源形容词，义为「活跃的」

senses.title: A performer on stage or screen
senses.definition: a person who performs a role in a play, film or show
senses.definitionCN: 在戏剧、电影或节目里扮演角色的人
senses.example: The actor learned his lines in a single week.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员只用一周就背熟了台词。
senses.why: Latin actor meant a doer; the stage borrowed it because a performer is literally one who does the part.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 actor 本指「做事的人」，舞台借它来指演员，因为演员字面上就是「把角色做出来的人」。

senses.title: A male performer
senses.definition: a man who performs a role, as contrasted with an actress
senses.definitionCN: 与女演员相对而言的男性表演者
senses.example: The actor and the actress swapped roles in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二幕里，男演员与女演员互换了角色。
senses.why: When actress was the usual word for a woman on stage, actor narrowed in contrast to mean the man.
senses.whyCN: 当 actress 成为女演员的常用词时，actor 便在对比中收窄为指男性。

senses.title: A person who takes part
senses.definition: a person or group that plays a part in an event or process
senses.definitionCN: 在某事件或过程中起作用的人或团体
senses.example: Several actors in the region signed the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的多个参与方签署了这份协议。
senses.why: The old sense of doer survives in politics, where actor means whoever acts on the stage of public affairs.
senses.whyCN: 「做事者」的古老义项在政治语境里活了下来：在公共事务的舞台上行动的一方就是 actor。

intro.en: A Latin word for a doer became the name of the person who does a role.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做事者」的拉丁词，变成了「把角色做出来的人」。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to do or to act.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、做、行动。

items.en: actor was simply a doer or a driver.
items.cn: actor 本义只是做事的人或推动者。

items.en: on the stage actor came to mean a performer.
items.cn: 在舞台上，actor 逐渐指表演者。

items.en: the word entered English for both a doer and a player.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时兼指做事者与演戏者。

items.en: politics keeps the older sense in phrases such as state actor.
items.cn: 政治语境用 state actor 这类说法保留了更古老的义项。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second names other people on a stage or in a deal.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的舞台或事务中的角色。

entries.definition: one who acts or causes change

normalIntro.en: act plus or: the doer of the act, on a stage or in a deal.
normalIntro.cn: act 加 or：做出动作的那个人，无论在舞台上还是在事务里。

normal.en: The or ending marks the doer, as in creator and director.
normal.cn: or 结尾表示做事的人，如 creator、director。

normal.en: Actor is now the neutral word; actress is used only for women.
normal.cn: 如今 actor 是中性说法，actress 只用于女性。

normal.en: Leading actor and supporting actor are the two award categories.
normal.cn: leading actor 与 supporting actor 是两个奖项类别。

normal.en: In politics an actor is any party that acts.
normal.cn: 在政治里，actor 指任何采取行动的一方。

normal.en: The plural actors adds a plain s.
normal.cn: 复数 actors 直接加 s。

abstract.en: See one figure alone under a single spotlight.
abstract.cn: 想象一束追光照着舞台中央的一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a contract table where several parties sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签约桌，几方依次落笔。

abstract.en: Think of a mask lifted at the end of a scene.
abstract.cn: 想象一场戏结束时被摘下的面具。

examples.en: He is a fine actor with a quiet voice.
examples.cn: 他是一位声音沉静的好演员。

examples.en: The actor refused to discuss the ending.
examples.cn: 这位演员拒绝谈论结局。

examples.en: Every actor in the deal wanted a share.
examples.cn: 这笔交易里的每一方都想分一杯羹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克特」——阿克特别会演，一上台就成了演员。

root: 拉丁语 actor（做事者），源自 agere（驱动、做）；由「做的人」引申为舞台上扮演角色的人，近代又分化出男演员与政治行动者二义。

sensesIntro.en: One old word for a doer now covers the stage, the male star and the political player.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个古老的「做事者」，如今同时指舞台上的演员、男主演与政治行动方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lone figure under a spotlight.
core.cn: 核心意象：追光下的一个人。

branches.en: the one who performs a role
the male half of a cast
branches.cn: 演员阵容里的男性一方

branches.en: a party that acts in public affairs
branches.cn: 在公共事务中行动的一方

branches.en: performer and man on stage
branches.cn: 表演者与舞台上的男性

branches.en: acting, on a stage or in a negotiation
branches.cn: 在舞台上或在谈判中「行动」

intro.en: A verb of doing plus a suffix for the doer.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的动词，加上表「做事者」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The same family gives action, active, agenda and agent.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词族还给出 action、active、agenda 与 agent。

definition_zh: 女演员；（口语）会做戏的女人
definition_en: a woman who performs in plays or films
core_image: 幕布拉开，一位女演员走到台前，灯光落在她脸上
scene: 灯光亮起，那位女演员从侧幕走到台前。The actress walked from the wings into the light.
sceneCN: 这里的 actress 是「女演员」（第 1 个义项：以表演为职业的女性）；句中指从侧幕走上台的那位。

pos.zh: 女演员；（口语）会做戏的女人

derivatives.zh: 去掉阴性后缀后的阳性形式，义为「演员；男演员」
同源动词，义为「表演；行动」
同源名词，义为「表演；演技」
同源名词，义为「行动」

senses.title: A woman who performs
senses.definition: a woman whose job is to perform in plays, films or shows
senses.definitionCN: 以在戏剧、电影或节目中表演为职业的女性
senses.example: The actress won the award twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这位女演员两次获得该奖。
senses.why: Actor plus the feminine ending ess named the woman on stage, a pattern that also produced waitress and hostess.
senses.whyCN: actor 加上阴性词尾 ess，就指舞台上的女性，同一构词法还造出了 waitress 与 hostess。

senses.title: A woman who puts on an act
senses.definition: a woman who hides her real feelings and pretends, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指掩饰真实情感、装模作样的女人
senses.example: Stop being such an actress and tell me the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 别演了，把实话告诉我。
senses.why: Because an actress plays a part for a living, the word was borrowed in speech for anyone who plays a part in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 女演员靠扮演角色为生，口语便借这个词来说日常生活中也在「演」的人。

intro.en: The Latin word for a doer took a feminine ending and entered English through French.
intro.cn: 表示「做事者」的拉丁词接上阴性词尾，经法语进入英语。

items.en: actor meant a doer, and actrix named a woman who did.
items.cn: actor 指做事者，actrix 指做事的女性。

items.en: the feminine suffix issa passed into popular Latin endings.
items.cn: 阴性词尾 issa 进入了通俗拉丁语的词尾系统。

items.en: actrice named a woman on the stage.
items.cn: actrice 指舞台上的女性表演者。

items.en: actress was coined in English on the model of French.
items.cn: actress 仿照法语在英语里被造出来。

items.en: many women now prefer actor, and actress survives mainly in awards.
items.cn: 如今许多女性更愿意用 actor，actress 主要留在奖项名称里。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second names women or performers in general.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的指女性或表演者的词。

normalIntro.en: actor plus ess: the same stage, marked as feminine.
normalIntro.cn: actor 加 ess：同一个舞台，标出女性。

normal.en: The ess ending also appears in waitress and hostess.
normal.cn: ess 结尾还见于 waitress 与 hostess。

normal.en: The plural actresses adds es because the word ends in s.
normal.cn: 复数 actresses 要加 es，因为词尾已有 s。

normal.en: Leading actress is still a standard award category.
normal.cn: leading actress 至今仍是标准奖项类别。

normal.en: Actor now works for both sexes, so actress is narrowing.
normal.cn: actor 如今两性通用，actress 的使用范围正在收窄。

normal.en: The second sense is spoken and mildly critical.
normal.cn: 第二个义项属口语，略带贬义。

abstract.en: See a curtain drawn back on a woman in the light.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布拉开，一位女性站在光里。

abstract.en: Picture a face changing expression the moment the door opens.
abstract.cn: 想象门一开，一张脸立刻换了表情。

abstract.en: Think of an award envelope opened on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上拆开一个获奖信封。

examples.en: She worked as an actress before turning director.
examples.cn: 她在转行做导演之前当过女演员。

examples.en: The actress refused to read the reviews.
examples.cn: 这位女演员拒绝去看那些评论。

examples.en: Do not be an actress with me; say what you feel.
examples.cn: 别在我面前做戏，有什么感觉就直说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克特瑞斯」——阿克特瑞斯小姐一上台，全场就知道她是女演员。

root: 由拉丁语 actor（做事者）加阴性词尾 -ess 构成；英语十六世纪仿法语 actrice 造出，本指舞台上的女性表演者，后在口语里引申为「会做戏的人」。

sensesIntro.en: One word names a woman on the stage and, in speech, a woman who plays a part in life.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指舞台上的女性，也在口语里指在生活中「演」的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman stepping into a pool of stage light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位女性走进舞台的光圈。

branches.en: a woman who performs for a living
a woman pretending in daily life
branches.cn: 在日常生活中装样子的女性

branches.en: the feminine half of a cast
branches.cn: 演员阵容中的女性一方

branches.en: playing a part, on stage or off
the spoken, mildly critical use

intro.en: A doer root, a feminine ending, and a woman on a stage.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做事者」的词根，加一个阴性词尾，得到舞台上的女性。

latinIntro.en: The family also gives actor, action, active and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族还给出 actor、action、active 与 agenda。

definition_en: existing in fact, or used to stress that something is the real thing
core_image: 一份报价单旁边摊着真实账单，数字比预想的大得多
scene: 账单一到，实际的费用比原先的报价高出一大截。The actual cost was far above the estimate.
sceneCN: 这里的 actual 是「实际的」（第 1 个义项：真实存在而非设想中的）；句中指真正结算出来的费用。

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「实际上；竟然」
加名词后缀 -ity，义为「现实性；实际情况」
加动词后缀 -ize，义为「实现、使成为现实」
同源基础动词，义为「行动」

senses.title: Existing in fact
senses.definition: existing in fact and not only in thought, in plan or in what was claimed
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在的，而不是只存在于想法、计划或别人的说法里
senses.example: No one knew the actual number of visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人知道访客的实际人数。
senses.why: The Latin base means a deed, so actual describes what has been done and can be pointed at, not what is merely said.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁词根指「做过的事」，所以 actual 描述的是已经做成、指得出来的东西，而不是嘴上说的东西。

senses.title: The real thing, not a copy
senses.definition: used to stress that something is the genuine thing rather than an imitation or a guess
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某物是原件本尊，而不是仿制品或猜测
senses.example: The actual painting hangs in the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画的真迹挂在隔壁房间里。
senses.why: Once actual marked what is real, speakers began using it to separate the genuine object from its copies and reports.
senses.whyCN: 既然 actual 标出「真的」，说话人就用它把真品与复制品、传闻区分开来，于是有了强调身份的用法。

intro.en: The word begins with a Latin noun for a deed and ends as an adjective of fact.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语里表示「行为」的名词出发，最后变成表示「事实」的形容词。

items.en: agere meant to drive or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: actus named a deed that had been carried out.
items.cn: actus 指已经完成的行为。

items.en: actualis described something belonging to deeds or to practice.
items.cn: actualis 形容与行为或实践有关的东西。

items.en: actuel shifted the sense towards what is real now.
items.cn: actuel 把词义推向「当下真实存在的」。

items.en: actual settled into the modern sense of real as opposed to supposed.
items.cn: actual 在英语里定型为「真实的」，与「设想的」相对。

note.en: The first group shares the act stem; the second names what is true rather than imagined.
note.cn: 第一组共享 act 词干；第二组是别的表示「真实而非想象」的词。

normalIntro.en: Actual is the adjective of the deed: what has really been done.
normalIntro.cn: actual 是「行为」的形容词：真被做出来的东西。

normal.en: The al ending is the same as in factual and natural.
normal.cn: al 结尾与 factual、natural 相同。

normal.en: Actual goes before the noun, as in actual cost.
normal.cn: actual 放在名词前，如 actual cost。

normal.en: In actual fact is a set phrase that repeats the idea twice.
normal.cn: in actual fact 是固定说法，等于把「事实」说了两遍。

normal.en: Do not confuse actual with current; the first means real, the second means now.
normal.cn: 别把 actual 与 current 搞混：前者是「真实」，后者是「当下」。

normal.en: The adverb is actually, not actualy.
normal.cn: 副词写作 actually，不要漏掉 l。

abstract.en: See a polished estimate torn beside a bigger real bill.
abstract.cn: 想象一份漂亮的报价单被撕开，旁边是更贵的真账单。

abstract.en: Picture a copy on the wall and the original in the vault.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上挂着复制品，真迹锁在库房里。

abstract.en: Think of a number checked twice against the record.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字被拿去和记录核对了两遍。

examples.en: The actual cost was far above the estimate.
examples.cn: 实际费用远高于估算。

examples.en: The actual painting hangs in the next room.
examples.cn: 那幅画的真迹挂在隔壁房间。

examples.en: Nobody could give the actual figure.
examples.cn: 谁也拿不出确切的数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克球」——阿克球场上到底踢得怎样，要看实际比分，不听传言。

root: 拉丁语 actualis（与行为有关的），源自 actus（行为）与 agere（做）；本义是「做出来的、可指认的」，由此变成「真实的、实际的」。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective marks what exists and, with stress, what is the genuine article.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形容词既标出真实存在，也能加重语气指「本尊」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a real bill placed beside a neat estimate.
core.cn: 核心意象：真实的账单摆在整洁的报价单旁边。

branches.en: what truly exists and can be counted
branches.cn: 真实存在、数得出来的东西

branches.en: the object itself rather than a copy
costs and figures as they turn out
branches.cn: 最终结算出来的费用与数字

branches.en: correcting a mistaken guess
fact and emphatic identity in one word
branches.cn: 事实与强调身份合在一个词里

intro.en: A deed root plus an adjective ending gives the sense of what is real.
intro.cn: 表示「行为」的词根加上形容词词尾，得到「真实的」这一含义。

latinIntro.en: The same root runs through action, actor and agency.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词根贯穿 action、actor 与 agency。

definition_en: used to state a fact, often one that corrects or surprises
core_image: 别人都在猜，一个人翻开账本把真实数字指出来
scene: 他嘴上说不在意，其实每天都在等那通电话。He said he did not care, but he actually waited for the call every day.
sceneCN: 这里的 actually 是「实际上」（第 1 个义项：说出与表面说法相反的真实情况）；句中揭出他真实的行为。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly，义为「实际的」
同源名词，义为「现实性；实际情况」
同源动词，义为「实现」

senses.title: In fact, contrary to appearances
senses.definition: used to give a fact that differs from what was said or assumed
senses.definitionCN: 用于说出与前述说法或表面印象不同的事实
senses.example: He said he was busy, but he actually stayed home.
senses.exampleCN: 他说自己很忙，实际上却待在家里。
senses.why: The adverb of actual reports what is really the case, and English uses it at the head of a sentence to correct the previous line.
senses.whyCN: actual 的副词是报告真实情况的，英语常把它放在句首，用来纠正上一句话。

senses.title: Surprisingly, even so
senses.definition: used to show surprise that something really happened
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事真的发生了，令人意外
senses.example: She actually finished the whole report in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 她竟然一夜之间写完了整份报告。
senses.why: Saying that something is actual can also express surprise, because the fact exceeds what the listener expected.
senses.whyCN: 强调某事「真的如此」，同时也表达了意外，因为这个事实超出了听者的预期。

senses.title: In real terms
senses.definition: used to describe what truly happened rather than what was planned or reported
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述真正发生的情况，而不是计划中或报道中的情况
senses.example: What did he actually say at the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上到底说了什么？
senses.why: Here the adverb sits inside the question and asks for the plain truth of an event, without any correcting tone.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词嵌在问句里，只是追问事件的真实内容，并不带纠正的语气。

intro.en: The adverb is simply actual plus the ordinary ly ending.
intro.cn: 这个副词就是 actual 加上常见的 ly 词尾。

items.en: actus named a deed, and actualis meant belonging to deeds.
items.cn: actus 指行为，actualis 意为与行为有关的。

items.en: actuel came to mean present and real.
items.cn: actuel 逐渐表示「当下的、真实的」。

items.en: actual took the sense of existing in fact.
items.cn: actual 取得「真实存在」的含义。

items.en: the ly form appeared as a plain adverb of manner.
items.cn: 加 ly 的形式出现，最初只是普通的方式副词。

items.en: in speech it became a common opener for corrections and surprises.
items.cn: 在口语里它成了引出纠正与意外的常用开头。

note.en: The first group shares the actual stem; the second gives other ways to state the truth.
note.cn: 第一组共享 actual 词干；第二组是别的陈述真相的说法。

normalIntro.en: Actual plus ly: the adverb that pulls a sentence back to the facts.
normalIntro.cn: actual 加 ly：把话拉回事实的那个副词。

normal.en: Use a comma after actually when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: actually 放在句首时后面要加逗号。

normal.en: In British speech it often softens a disagreement.
normal.cn: 在英式口语里它常用来缓和不同意见。

normal.en: Actually is not the same as currently; the first is about truth, the second about time.
normal.cn: actually 与 currently 不同：前者讲真假，后者讲时间。

normal.en: The stress can fall on ac, which sharpens the surprise.
normal.cn: 重音可以落在 ac 上，意外感更强。

normal.en: Remember the l in the middle: actually, not actualy.
normal.cn: 记住中间那个 l：是 actually。

abstract.en: See someone open a ledger while others keep guessing.
abstract.cn: 想象别人还在猜，有人已经翻开账本。

abstract.en: Picture a raised eyebrow after an unexpected result.
abstract.cn: 想象一个出乎意料的结果让人挑起眉毛。

abstract.en: Think of a witness correcting a report line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象证人一行行纠正报道里的说法。

examples.en: Actually, I have never met him before.
examples.cn: 其实我以前从没见过他。

examples.en: The medicine actually worked within an hour.
examples.cn: 这药竟然一小时之内就见效了。

examples.en: Nobody asked what actually happened that night.
examples.cn: 没有人追问那天夜里到底发生了什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克球累」——阿克球打累了，才说出实情：其实他一直在硬撑。

root: 由 actual（实际的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；actual 出自拉丁语 actualis（与行为有关的），因此这个词的核心始终是「事情真实的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb corrects, one expresses surprise, and one simply asks for the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词，一种用来纠正，一种表示意外，一种只是追问真相。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger opened while others still guess.
core.cn: 核心意象：别人还在猜，账本已经翻开。

branches.en: a fact that contradicts the last remark
branches.cn: 与上一句话相反的事实

branches.en: a result that exceeds expectation
a plain question about what occurred
branches.cn: 追问事情本来面目的问句

branches.en: truth stated versus truth asked for
surprise built on a real event
branches.cn: 建立在真实事件上的意外

intro.en: An adjective of fact takes the most common adverb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示事实的形容词，接上最常见的副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The family also gives action, actor and agency.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族还给出 action、actor 与 agency。

definition_zh: 急性的；敏锐的；严重的；锐角的
definition_en: sharp, severe, or sudden in onset
core_image: 一根针尖闪出寒光，尖端细得几乎看不见
scene: 医生判断这是急性阑尾炎，要求立刻安排手术。The doctor called it acute appendicitis and ordered surgery at once.
sceneCN: 这里的 acute 是「急性的」（第 1 个义项：发病急、病程短的疾病类型）；句中指急需处理的阑尾炎。

pos.zh: 急性的；敏锐的；严重的；锐角的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「强烈地；敏锐地」
加名词后缀 -ness，义为「敏锐；剧烈」
同源名词，义为「（感官的）敏锐度」
同源名词，义为「精明、洞察力」

senses.title: A disease that comes sharply
senses.definition: describing an illness that begins suddenly and is short but severe
senses.definitionCN: 形容发病突然、病程较短但症状较重的疾病
senses.example: The doctor called it acute appendicitis.
senses.exampleCN: 医生称之为急性阑尾炎。
senses.why: Latin acutus meant sharpened, and physicians used it for a disease whose onset cuts in sharply rather than creeping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acutus 意为「磨尖的」，医生用它形容来势像刀割一样突然、而不是慢慢拖的病。

senses.title: A very sharp sense or mind
senses.definition: able to notice or understand things quickly and clearly
senses.definitionCN: 能够迅速而清楚地察觉或理解事物的
senses.example: Dogs have an acute sense of smell.
senses.exampleCN: 狗的嗅觉非常敏锐。
senses.why: A sharpened edge cuts easily, so the same image was applied to hearing, sight and judgement that cut to the point.
senses.whyCN: 磨尖的刃容易切开东西，于是同一意象被用到听觉、视觉与判断力上：一下就切中要害。

senses.title: Severe and urgent
senses.definition: very serious and needing quick attention
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重、需要立即处理的
senses.example: The city faces an acute shortage of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临严重缺水。
senses.why: If a condition is sharp, it hurts now, so acute shifted from sudden illness to any problem at its most intense.
senses.whyCN: 状况「尖锐」就意味着当下就疼，于是 acute 从突然发病扩展到任何处于最紧张程度的问题。

senses.title: An angle below ninety degrees
senses.definition: describing an angle smaller than a right angle
senses.definitionCN: 形容小于直角的角
senses.example: The two lines meet at an acute angle.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条线以一个锐角相交。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest sense: an acute angle is the sharpest kind of corner, the one that looks like a point.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了最古老的含义：锐角是最尖的一类角，看上去就像一个针尖。

intro.en: The word starts from the Latin name for a needle and the verb to sharpen.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语里「针」的名称和「磨尖」的动词出发。

items.en: acus meant a needle.
items.cn: acus 意为针。

items.en: acuere meant to sharpen or to whet.
items.cn: acuere 意为磨尖、磨快。

items.en: acutus described anything sharpened, including pain and fever.
items.cn: acutus 形容一切被磨尖的东西，包括疼痛与发热。

items.en: acute entered medicine for sharp fevers and later for sharp senses.
items.cn: acute 先进入医学，指来势凶的发热，后来才指敏锐的感官。

items.en: geometry added the acute angle, the sharpest corner of all.
items.cn: 几何学又添上「锐角」，即最尖的那种角。

note.en: The first group shares the sharp root; the second names other ways of being intense.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「尖」的词根；第二组是别的表示「强烈」的词。

normalIntro.en: Sharp is the single picture behind the illness, the mind and the angle.
normalIntro.cn: 「尖」是贯穿疾病、心思与角度的同一个画面。

normal.en: Acute and chronic are a pair: sharp and short against long and slow.
normal.cn: acute 与 chronic 是一对：急而短，对慢而长。

normal.en: An acute angle is under ninety degrees, the sharp one.
normal.cn: 锐角小于九十度，是最尖的那个角。

normal.en: The noun acuity keeps the same sharp idea.
normal.cn: 名词 acuity 保留了同样的「尖锐」。

normal.en: The comparative uses more, because the word is long.
normal.cn: 这个词较长，比较级用 more。

normal.en: Do not confuse acute with a cute, which is far softer.
normal.cn: 别把 acute 与 cute 混同，后者语气柔软得多。

abstract.en: See a needle point catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针尖在光下闪出亮线。

abstract.en: Picture a sudden pain that makes a person stop walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵突如其来的痛让人停住脚步。

abstract.en: Think of two lines closing to a narrow point.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线收拢成一个很窄的尖角。

examples.en: He felt acute pain in his chest.
examples.cn: 他感到胸口一阵剧痛。

examples.en: Her acute hearing caught the whisper across the room.
examples.cn: 她敏锐的听觉捕捉到了房间另一头的低语。

examples.en: The region faces an acute shortage of doctors.
examples.cn: 这个地区严重缺乏医生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q特」——阿Q特别敏感，一点风吹草动就觉得疼，医生说是急性发作。

root: 拉丁语 acutus（磨尖的），源自 acuere（磨快）与 acus（针）；由「尖」这一核心意象分出四个方向：发病急、感官敏锐、问题严重、角小于直角。

sensesIntro.en: One sharp image branches into illness, perception, severity and geometry.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「尖」的意象，分叉到疾病、感知、严重程度与几何。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle point shining in the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：光下闪亮的针尖。

branches.en: an illness that cuts in suddenly
senses that catch the smallest detail
branches.cn: 能捕捉最细小动静的感官

branches.en: a problem at its most intense
branches.cn: 处于最紧张程度的问题

branches.en: a corner narrowed to a point
sharpness shared by illness and crisis
branches.cn: 疾病与危机共有的「尖锐」

intro.en: A needle root plus a Latin participle ending gives the sense of sharpened.
intro.cn: 表示「针」的词根加上拉丁分词词尾，得到「被磨尖的」。

latinIntro.en: The same root gives acumen, acuity and acupuncture.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词根还给出 acumen、acuity 与 acupuncture。

definition_en: to change yourself or something else to fit new conditions
core_image: 一件旧外套被改短袖口，正好合上新主人的身
scene: 搬到北方以后，一家人很快适应了干冷的冬天。The family adapted quickly to the dry cold winter.
sceneCN: 这里的 adapted 是「适应」（第 1 个义项：改变自己以配合新条件）；句中指一家人适应北方的气候。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「适应；改编作品」
加形容词后缀 -able，义为「能适应的」
由 adaptable 加 -ity，义为「适应性」
加表施动者的 -er，义为「适配器；改编者」

senses.title: To fit into a new setting
senses.definition: to change your behaviour or habits so as to fit new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变自己的行为或习惯，以配合新的环境与条件
senses.example: Children adapt to a new school faster than adults.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子比大人更快适应新学校。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to fit something to something, and the first thing people fit is themselves to a new place.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「使一物合于另一物」，而人最先要去合的，就是自己与新环境。

senses.title: To turn a book into a film
senses.definition: to change a book, play or story so that it can be performed or filmed
senses.definitionCN: 把书、剧本或故事改写，使其能被演出或拍成影视
senses.example: The novel was adapted for the screen last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说去年被改编成了电影。
senses.why: A story must be fitted to a new medium, and English borrowed the same verb for that act of fitting.
senses.whyCN: 故事必须被「装进」另一种媒介，英语就用同一个「使适合」的动词来指这件事。

senses.title: To change a thing for a new use
senses.definition: to change a building or object so that it can serve a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改造建筑或物品，使其能用于另一种用途
senses.example: They adapted the barn into a small studio.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把谷仓改造成了一间小工作室。
senses.why: Here the object, not the person, is fitted to a purpose, which is why the verb takes a direct object and a new function.
senses.whyCN: 这里被「使适合」的是物而不是人，所以动词直接带宾语，并接上新的用途。

intro.en: A Latin verb made of a prefix meaning to and a verb meaning to fit.
intro.cn: 这个拉丁动词由一个表「朝向」的前缀和一个表「使贴合」的动词组成。

items.en: aptus meant fitted or suitable.
items.cn: aptus 意为合适的、贴合好的。

items.en: aptare meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: aptare 意为使一物贴合一物。

items.en: adaptare added the prefix ad, meaning towards.
items.cn: adaptare 加上前缀 ad，表示「朝向」。

items.en: adapter carried the verb into French with the same sense.
items.cn: adapter 把这一动词带进法语，含义不变。

items.en: adapt entered English, and later took on the sense of rewriting for stage or screen.
items.cn: adapt 进入英语，后来又发展出为舞台或银幕改写的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the apt root; the second names other ways of making something fit.
note.cn: 第一组共享 apt 词根；第二组是别的表示「使适合」的词。

normalIntro.en: ad towards, apt fit: to fit towards something new.
normalIntro.cn: ad 表朝向，apt 表贴合：朝着新情况去贴合。

normal.en: Adapt to is followed by a noun or an ing form.
normal.cn: adapt to 后面接名词或动名词。

normal.en: Adapt from names the source, adapt for names the medium.
normal.cn: adapt from 指来源，adapt for 指所服务的媒介。

normal.en: Do not mix adapt with adopt; the second means to take as one's own.
normal.cn: 别把 adapt 与 adopt 混用，后者是「采纳、收养」。

normal.en: The adjective adaptable takes able at the end.
normal.cn: 形容词 adaptable 在词尾接 able。

normal.en: Biology uses adaptation for a trait that fits a habitat.
normal.cn: 生物学用 adaptation 指适应栖息地的性状。

abstract.en: See a coat taken in at the sleeves to fit a smaller wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套把袖口收窄，正好给更小的人穿。

abstract.en: Picture a book opened beside a film script.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书摊开在电影剧本旁边。

abstract.en: Think of a barn with new windows and a studio inside.
abstract.cn: 想象谷仓装上新的窗子，里面成了工作室。

examples.en: It takes time to adapt to a new climate.
examples.cn: 适应新的气候需要时间。

examples.en: The story was adapted into a short play.
examples.cn: 这个故事被改编成了一出短剧。

examples.en: They adapted the old mill into a museum.
examples.cn: 他们把这座旧磨坊改造成了博物馆。

scene: 这一版改编把故事搬到了一座海边小镇。This adaptation moves the story to a small seaside town.
sceneCN: 这里的 adaptation 是「改编作品」（第 2 个义项：为另一种媒介改写后的成品）；句中指这一版改写的电影。

senses.title: The process of fitting in
senses.definition: the process of changing in order to deal with new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为应对新条件而做出改变的过程
senses.example: Her adaptation to city life took several months.
senses.exampleCN: 她适应城市生活花了好几个月。
senses.why: The noun of adapt names the whole process, not a single change, which is why it often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: adapt 的名词指整个「变得合适」的过程，而不是某一次改动，所以常与 to 连用。

senses.title: A work rewritten for a new medium
senses.definition: a film, play or show made from a book or other source
senses.definitionCN: 根据书或其他来源改写的电影、戏剧或节目
senses.example: The film is a loose adaptation of a Russian novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是对一部俄国小说的松散改编。
senses.why: When a book is fitted to the screen, the finished product itself came to be called an adaptation.
senses.whyCN: 当一本书被「装进」银幕，改出来的成品本身也就叫 adaptation。

senses.title: A trait that helps survival
senses.definition: a feature or behaviour that helps a living thing survive in its habitat
senses.definitionCN: 帮助生物在栖息地存活下来的身体特征或行为
senses.example: Thick fur is an adaptation to extreme cold.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的毛皮是对极寒的一种适应。
senses.why: Biology took the everyday word and made it name the result of fitting that evolution keeps.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个日常词，用来指进化保留下来的「贴合环境」的结果。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun built on the verb meaning to fit to.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语里建立在「使适合」动词上的行为名词。

items.en: aptus meant fit or suitable.
items.cn: aptus 意为合适的、贴合的。

items.en: adaptare meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: adaptare 意为使一物贴合另一物。

items.en: adaptatio named the act of fitting.
items.cn: adaptatio 指「使贴合」这一行为。

items.en: adaptation carried the noun into French.
items.cn: adaptation 把这个名词带进法语。

items.en: English first used it for biology, then for rewritten plays.
items.cn: 英语先用它讲生物，后来才用它指改写的剧本。

normalIntro.en: adapt plus ation: the whole process, the finished work, and the trait that survives.
normalIntro.cn: adapt 加 ation：既是过程，也是成品，还是活下来的性状。

normal.en: The ending ation usually names an action or its result, as in creation.
normal.cn: ation 结尾通常指行为或其结果，如 creation。

normal.en: Film adaptation and stage adaptation are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: film adaptation 与 stage adaptation 是固定说法。

normal.en: In biology, adaptation is countable: one trait, two traits.
normal.cn: 在生物学里 adaptation 可数：一种性状，两种性状。

normal.en: Adaptation to is followed by the new condition.
normal.cn: adaptation to 后面接所适应新条件。

normal.en: The verb is adapt; do not drop the second a.
normal.cn: 动词是 adapt，别漏掉第二个 a。

abstract.cn: 想象一本写满批注的小说旁边放着电影分镜。

abstract.en: Picture a foreign student learning local table manners.
abstract.cn: 想象一位外国学生学当地的餐桌礼节。

abstract.en: Think of thick fur on an animal in deep snow.
abstract.cn: 想象厚雪里一只动物身上厚厚的毛。

examples.en: Adaptation to the new rules was slow at first.
examples.cn: 起初对新规则的适应很慢。

examples.en: The play is an adaptation of a famous diary.
examples.cn: 这出戏改编自一本著名日记。

examples.en: Long legs are an adaptation for running fast.
examples.cn: 长腿是跑得快的一种适应。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，同时指过程、成品与性状。

definition_zh: 添加；把……相加；补充说；增添
definition_en: to put something together with something else, or to say something more
core_image: 一只手把一勺糖倒进已经满到杯口的茶里
scene: 汤有点淡，她又往锅里加了一小撮盐。She added a pinch of salt to the soup.
sceneCN: 这里的 added 是「添加」（第 1 个义项：把一物放进另一物里）；句中指往汤里再加盐。

senses.title: To put one thing into another
senses.definition: to put something together with something else so that the amount grows
senses.definitionCN: 把一物与另一物放在一起，使数量增加
senses.example: She added a little sugar to the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她往茶里加了一点糖。
senses.why: Latin addere is ad plus dare, to give to, so adding is literally giving something to what is already there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addere 是 ad 加 dare，即「给到……上」，所以添加就是往已有的东西上再给一点。

senses.title: To put numbers together
senses.definition: to put two or more numbers together to get a total
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数合在一起求得总数
senses.example: Add these figures and tell me the total.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些数字加起来，告诉我总数。
senses.why: Arithmetic takes the physical act of putting things together and applies it to numbers, which are treated as objects.
senses.whyCN: 算术把「把东西放到一起」这个物理动作搬到数字上，因为数字在运算里被当作可搬动的对象。

senses.title: To say something more
senses.definition: to say something further after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 在已经说过的话之后再说一些
senses.example: She added that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充说办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: Speech is treated as a pile to which one more remark can be added, which is why the verb takes a that clause.
senses.whyCN: 话语被当成一堆可以再添一句的东西，所以这个动词后面能接 that 从句。

senses.title: To make a situation stronger
senses.definition: to make a feeling or problem greater
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情绪或问题变得更强、更严重
senses.example: The delay only added to our worries.
senses.exampleCN: 这场延误只是增添了我们担忧。
senses.why: With the preposition to, the verb no longer adds an object but adds weight to a state, often a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 接上介词 to 时，动词不再是加一件东西，而是给某种状态（往往是坏状态）加分量。

intro.en: The Latin verb is a compound of to and give.
intro.cn: 这个拉丁动词由「朝向」和「给」两部分合成。

items.en: dare meant to give.
items.cn: dare 意为给。

items.cn: ad 意为朝向、到。

items.cn: addere 意为「给到……上」，因此引申为加入、增添。

items.en: add entered English for joining one thing to another.
items.cn: add 进入英语，指把一物加到另一物上。

items.en: it spread to arithmetic and to the act of saying more.
items.cn: 它又扩展到算术运算与「再说几句」的用法。

note.en: The first group shares the add stem; the second names other ways of putting in more.
note.cn: 第一组共享 add 词干；第二组是别的表示「再加进去」的词。

normalIntro.en: ad towards, dare give: to give something towards a pile.
normalIntro.cn: ad 表朝向，dare 表给：朝着已有的一堆再给一点。

normal.cn: 过去式要双写 d：added。

normal.en: Add to is followed by the thing that grows, not the thing you put in.
normal.cn: add to 后面接被加重的东西，而不是你放进去的东西。

normal.en: Add up has two senses: to total, and to make sense.
normal.cn: add up 有两义：合计，以及「说得通」。

normal.en: Add that introduces reported speech.
normal.cn: add that 用于引述别人补充的话。

normal.en: The noun is addition, with a single d.

definition_en: the condition of being unable to stop using something or doing something
core_image: 一个人反复伸手去拿同一只杯子，明知不该却停不下来
scene: 他花了一年才摆脱对止痛药的依赖。It took him a year to beat his addiction to painkillers.

senses.title: Dependence on a substance
senses.definition: a strong need for a drug or drink that is very hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 对药物或酒类的强烈需求，极难戒断
senses.example: His addiction to painkillers began after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 他对止痛药的依赖始于那场车祸。
senses.why: Latin addictio meant handing someone over, and a person given over to a drug was later said to have an addiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addictio 指把某人交付出去；当一个人被「交付」给某种药物，后来就说他有了 addiction。

senses.title: Being hooked on an activity
senses.definition: a strong habit of doing something that one cannot easily give up
senses.definitionCN: 难以轻易放弃的强烈习惯，对象是某项活动而非物质
senses.example: His addiction to video games worried his parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他对电子游戏的沉迷让父母担忧。
senses.why: As the word spread beyond drugs, the same loss of control was applied to games, work and shopping.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词走出药物范围，「失去控制」的同样情形就被用到了游戏、工作与购物上。

intro.en: The word began in Roman law, where it meant handing a person over.
intro.cn: 这个词起于罗马法，本义是把一个人交付出去。

items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣告。

items.cn: addiction 最初指对某种习惯或事务的投入。

normalIntro.cn: addict 加 ion：被交给某物之后所处的状态。

normal.cn: 常见搭配是 addiction to 某物。

normal.en: Drug addiction and alcohol addiction are the two medical staples.
normal.cn: drug addiction 与 alcohol addiction 是医学上的两个基本说法。

normal.en: The person is an addict, the state is addiction.
normal.cn: 人叫 addict，状态叫 addiction。

normal.en: Do not confuse addiction with addition; the second is simple arithmetic.

senses.title: The act of adding
senses.definition: the act of putting something together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某物与另一物放在一起的行为
senses.example: The addition of a porch changed the whole house.
senses.exampleCN: 加建一个门廊改变了整栋房子。
senses.why: Latin additio is simply the noun of the act, so this sense names the deed rather than the thing produced.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 additio 就是这个动作的名词，因此这一义项指「做的事」，而不是做出来的东西。

senses.title: Adding numbers
senses.definition: the arithmetic process of putting numbers together to get a total
senses.definitionCN: 把数合起来求总数的算术运算
senses.example: The children are learning addition and subtraction.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们正在学加法和减法。
senses.why: Arithmetic named its four basic processes with Latin nouns, and addition kept the plain sense of putting together.
senses.whyCN: 算术用拉丁名词给四种基本运算命名，addition 保留了「并到一起」这一朴素含义。

senses.title: A thing or person added
senses.definition: a person or thing that is added to a group or a place
senses.definitionCN: 被添进某个群体或某个地方的人或物
senses.example: The baby is the newest addition to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个婴儿是家里最新添的成员。
senses.why: English often turns a process noun into a countable thing, so the result of adding becomes an addition itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把过程名词变成可数的东西，于是「添加的结果」本身也叫 an addition。

definition_en: extra, or added to what already exists
core_image: 账单末尾又多出一行收费，金额不大却躲不开
scene: 航班取消后，航空公司安排了酒店，却要另收一笔额外费用。The airline offered a hotel but charged an additional fee.
sceneCN: 这里的 additional 是「额外的」（第 1 个义项：在原有之外再加上的）；句中指在原价之外另收的钱。

senses.title: More of the same kind
senses.definition: more than what was already there or already agreed
senses.definitionCN: 比原有的或原先约定的更多
senses.example: The airline charged an additional fee for the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司为这件行李另收了一笔费用。
senses.why: The adjective of addition simply marks something joined onto an existing amount, so it always implies a second portion.
senses.whyCN: addition 的形容词只表示「被并到已有数量上」，所以它总含「再来一份」的意思。

senses.title: Filling out what is missing
senses.definition: given to complete or support what is already known
senses.definitionCN: 为使已有内容更完整而提供的
senses.example: Please send any additional information by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前把补充材料寄来。
senses.why: Here what is added does not raise a number but fills a gap, which is why the word pairs with information and support.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「加」不是把数字抬高，而是把缺口补上，所以常与 information、support 搭配。

definition_en: used to add another point, or in an extra way
core_image: 一篇报告的末尾又补上一段「还有一点」
scene: 票价之外，乘客还要为行李另外付费。Additionally, passengers pay for their luggage.

senses.title: Here is one more point
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to add a further point
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，引出另一条补充的信息
senses.example: Additionally, the museum closes on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，博物馆每周一闭馆。
senses.why: The adverb of additional marks a point joined to the list already given, so it works as a connector.
senses.whyCN: additional 的副词表示「又并进一条」，所以它天然充当连接词。

senses.title: In an extra way
senses.definition: in a way that is charged or supplied on top of the usual amount
senses.definitionCN: 以在通常数额之外另行收取或提供的方式
senses.example: The room was additionally charged for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 这间房的早餐是额外收费的。
senses.why: In this use the adverb modifies the verb rather than linking sentences, so it describes how the charge is made.
senses.whyCN: 这种用法里副词修饰的是动词而不是连接句子，描述的是「以何种方式收费」。

definition_en: the details of where someone lives, a formal speech, or to deal with a matter
core_image: 一封信的正面写着收件人的名字与门牌号
scene: 会议开始前，主席起身向全体代表致辞。The chairman rose to address the delegates.
sceneCN: 这里的 address 是「致辞」（第 2 个义项：面向听众发表正式讲话）；句中指向全体代表讲话。

senses.title: Where someone can be found
senses.definition: the details of a place where a person lives or a business is located
senses.definitionCN: 某人居住或某机构所在的详细地点信息
senses.example: Write your home address at the top of the form.
senses.exampleCN: 在表格顶端写下你的家庭住址。
senses.why: French addresser meant to direct something to a place, so the place directed to became the address.
senses.whyCN: 法语 addresser 意为把东西指送到某处，被指送到的那个地方就成了 address。

senses.title: A formal speech
senses.definition: a formal speech given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众发表的正式讲话
senses.example: The chairman rose to address the delegates.
senses.exampleCN: 主席起身向代表们致辞。
senses.why: To address a meeting first meant to direct words towards it, and the noun then named the speech itself.
senses.whyCN: address a meeting 本指把话「指向」会场，名词随后就指那篇讲话本身。

senses.title: The name you call someone
senses.definition: the title or name used when speaking or writing to a person
senses.definitionCN: 当面或书面称呼某人时使用的头衔或名字
senses.example: He prefers the address Doctor to Mister.
senses.exampleCN: 他更喜欢别人称他博士而不是先生。
senses.why: Directing words at a person includes choosing how to name them, so address came to mean the form of words used.
senses.whyCN: 把话指向某人，也包括选择怎么叫他，于是 address 又指所用的称谓。

senses.title: To deal with a problem
senses.definition: to give attention to a problem and try to solve it
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力放到某个问题上并设法解决
senses.example: The report failed to address the real cause.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告没有触及真正的原因。
senses.why: Turning your attention towards a problem is a kind of directing, which is why address took this modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 把注意力「转向」一个问题也是一种指送，所以 address 发展出这一现代义项。

senses.title: To send something to a place
senses.definition: to write a name and place on an envelope or parcel and send it
senses.definitionCN: 在信封或包裹上写清姓名与地点并寄出
senses.example: The letter was addressed to a hotel in Rome.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信是寄往罗马一家酒店的。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: putting a direction on a thing so that it travels there.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实义：在东西上写下方向，让它能去到那个地方。

intro.en: A French verb of directing, worn down into one English word with five senses.
intro.cn: 一个法语中表示「指向」的动词，在英语里磨成一个拥有五个义项的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base also gives direct, direction and dress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基还给出 direct、direction 与 dress。

definition_en: enough in amount, or just good enough in quality
core_image: 一只水杯正好倒到刻度线，不多也不少
scene: 这点工资够维持基本生活，却谈不上宽裕。The salary is adequate for basic needs but no more.
sceneCN: 这里的 adequate 是「足够的」（第 1 个义项：数量上刚好满足需要）；句中指工资刚好够用。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -acy，义为「足够；适当」
加副词后缀 -ly，义为「充分地」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「不足的」

senses.title: Enough for the need
senses.definition: enough in amount for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上足以满足某个用途
senses.example: The room has adequate space for ten people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有足够的空间容纳十个人。
senses.why: Latin adaequare means to make equal, so adequate describes a supply brought level with the demand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adaequare 意为「使相等」，所以 adequate 描述的是供给被拉到与需求齐平。

senses.title: Just good enough
senses.definition: acceptable in quality but not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 质量上可以接受，但算不上出色
senses.example: His work is adequate, though hardly brilliant.
senses.exampleCN: 他的工作还算合格，但谈不上出色。
senses.why: Once the word meant level with a standard, it also judged quality, and level with the bar is only just enough.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词表示「与标准齐平」，它也能评价质量；而与标准线齐平，就意味着「刚够」。

intro.en: The word is Latin for making equal, built from a prefix and the word for equal.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里意为「使相等」，由一个前缀和表示「相等」的词构成。

items.en: aequus meant equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等的、平的。

items.en: adaequare meant to make equal to.
items.cn: adaequare 意为使与……相等。

items.en: adaequatus described something made level with a need.
items.cn: adaequatus 形容被拉到与需求齐平的东西。

items.en: adequate entered English as a word of proportion.
items.cn: adequate 作为表示比例相称的词进入英语。

items.en: it now also means no more than acceptable.
items.cn: 如今它也指「仅仅过得去」。

note.en: The first group shares the equal root; the second names other degrees of enough.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「相等」的词根；第二组是别的表示「够」的词。

normalIntro.en: ad towards, aequus equal: brought level with what is needed.
normalIntro.cn: ad 表朝向，aequus 表相等：被拉到与需求齐平。

normal.en: Adequate for is followed by the purpose or the person.
normal.cn: adequate for 后面接用途或对象。

normal.en: It often carries a faint hint of only just enough.
normal.cn: 它常带一点「刚刚够」的意味。

normal.en: The negative is inadequate, with the prefix in-.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 inadequate，前缀为 in-。

normal.en: The noun is adequacy, not adequateness.
normal.cn: 名词通常用 adequacy。

normal.en: The comparative takes more, since the word is long.
normal.cn: 词形较长，比较级用 more。

abstract.en: See water poured exactly to a marked line.
abstract.cn: 想象水正好倒到刻度线。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that holds but does not shine.
abstract.cn: 想象一座承得住却并不漂亮的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a test paper marked just passing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张刚好及格的试卷。

examples.en: We need adequate time to finish the survey.
examples.cn: 我们需要足够的时间完成这项调查。

examples.en: The shelter provides adequate food and bedding.
examples.cn: 收容所提供充足的食物与被褥。

examples.en: His answer was adequate but not convincing.
examples.cn: 他的回答尚可，却不足以服人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪夸特」——阿迪夸口说准备得足够，结果一查，刚好够用。

root: 拉丁语 adaequatus（使相等的），源自 adaequare（使与……相等）与 aequus（相等的）；由「供给与需求拉平」引申为足够，再由「与标准齐平」引申为尚可。

sensesIntro.en: Level with the need means enough; level with the bar means barely acceptable.
sensesIntro.cn: 与需求齐平是足够；与标准齐平，就只是勉强合格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water poured exactly to the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：水正好倒到刻度线。

branches.en: a supply brought level with demand
branches.cn: 供给被拉到与需求齐平

branches.en: quality that only meets the bar
branches.cn: 仅仅达到标准线的质量

branches.en: space and time just enough for the task
branches.cn: 刚好够用的空间与时间

branches.en: work that passes without praise
branches.cn: 过关但得不到称赞的工作

branches.en: quantity and quality both measured against a line
branches.cn: 数量与质量都以一条线来衡量

intro.en: A prefix of direction plus the Latin word for equal, made into a participle.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀，加上拉丁语「相等」，再变成分词形式。

latinIntro.en: Aequus also gives equal, equity and equator.
latinIntro.cn: aequus 还给出 equal、equity 与 equator。
